A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 12 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original STEU/STEM evaluations, demographic analyses, memory-injection comparisons, and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds DPO experiments, human persona evaluation, and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: v1 investigates memory-induced bias without proposing mitigation. v2 introduces a preference-data construction and filtering procedure followed by DPO fine-tuning to resist irrelevant persona information (Section 5, Appendix F). The original memory-injection procedure is retained.

E1.justification: Beyond retained STEU/STEM coverage, v2 adds Tulu3-based preference training, MMLU and instruction-following evaluation, and persona-realism judgments. LongBench and WildChat supply preceding contexts for new STEU scenarios, while Appendix G adds controlled demographic conditions.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 model set and FAISS/system comparators remain unchanged. New Table 2 introduces Gemma-2-2B and Qwen-3-1.7B base-model controls for DPO. Tables 3–4 additionally report R1-Distill-Llama in demographic comparisons, where v1 Figure 3 did not identify that comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include DPO training on 500 instances, zero-shot MMLU evaluation, context experiments reporting 780 questions per condition, and demographic tests using 10 augmented profiles. The reported reference age also changes from 25–34 to 34–65 in Section 3, while new tables specify 35–64; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds persona-realism validation, long-context and conversation-history tests, sentiment/readability/token-length confound analyses, and controlled income, education, and disability comparisons (Appendices B.1 and G). The original memory-injection ablation and error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 expands demographic reporting with tabulated standard errors and exact p-values, and specifies t-tests and Pearson correlations for new analyses. Confidence intervals and variation across personas were already reported in v1. No increase in repeated runs or seeds is established.

E6.justification: Original performance and error-distribution tables retain their values. New results include DPO outcomes, context-conditioned scores, persona-realism judgments, and additional demographic/confound findings. For example, v2 Table 2 reports Gemma STEU accuracy of 53.30% before DPO and 63.70% afterward, alongside instruction-following scores falling from 59.50% to 55.40%; these are newly reported experiments.

T1.justification: The mixed-effects equation, Gaussian random-effect assumption, and mathematical specification are unchanged, moving from v1 Appendix D to v2 Appendix A. v2 adds no formal DPO derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The original claims about memory-induced emotional bias remain. v2 adds a central contribution in its abstract and introduction: a general-purpose preference dataset for mitigation, supported by a new claim that targeted DPO can reduce persona-induced disparities.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning deployment auditing, semantic versus surface-text explanations of bias, and the relevance of additional demographic dimensions. It discusses DPO's instruction-following tradeoff. However, Section 7 still states that no mitigation strategy was proposed, conflicting with the new mitigation section.

D1.justification: v2 adds code and dataset links, persona-evaluation annotation details, and DPO implementation information, including generator/judge identities, filtering rules, three training epochs, learning rate 5e-6, and warmup ratio 0.1. Existing inference settings largely remain, but v1's identification of DeepSeek-R1 as the persona generator is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting Tulu3 training, MMLU, LongBench, WildChat, reward filtering, and socioeconomic/disability analyses, while removing the WritingBench citation. The original positioning around personalization, emotional intelligence, and Bourdieu's framework remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits persona-generation and annotation explanations, revises the conclusion, and reorders existing appendices with a contents page. The original research questions and most main-text narrative remain; much of the expansion consists of new scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 changes appendix prose from two columns to one, reorganizes existing displays, and adds eight tables covering DPO, demographic coefficients, contextual conditions, and demographic tests. All five original figure images are retained, with some relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful mitigation, robustness, and reproducibility material beyond v1's audit. However, important new evidence is internally inconsistent: demographic model attributions conflict with retained Figure 3, and Table 3 reports p = 0.134 alongside a 95% interval excluding zero. The 93% realism comparison also names PersonaHub in the main text but PRISM in Appendix B.1. These reliability problems prevent a confident assessment of net quality improvement.
